--- title: "Week 16" author: "Victoria Sjalim" date: "2026-11-8" format: html execute: freeze: auto --- # Updates - Check Validation Pipeline Tab --> easier to understand - Categorized FP and FN more thoroughly # FN and FP reasons Each row of `relations.tsv` now has only three statuses (**TP**, **FN**, **FP**) and a separate **reason** for FN and FP, so each reason points at one kind of bug. The reasons are checked in this order: | Status | Reason | Meaning | |---|---|---| | FN | `wrong_side` | its own IS reports the CDS, but only on the other side | | FN | `wrong_IS` | only a differently named IS reports the CDS, on the same side | | FN | `not_found` | not reported at all (see the miss cause below) | | FP | `unplaceable` | eris's nearest gene cannot be placed on the reference | | FP | `wrong_side` | a truth CDS of its IS, but on the other side | | FP | `wrong_IS` | a truth CDS on the same side, but of a differently named IS | | FP | `not_in_truth` | in no truth relation | Precision, recall and F1 are unchanged, only the labels are new. ::: {#51bce866 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd RESULTS = "../result/eris_validation" ASSEMBLIES = {"complete": "Complete genome (FASTA)", "simulated": "Simulated GFA", "real": "Real-reads GFA"} pd.set_option("display.max_rows", None, "display.max_columns", None, "display.max_colwidth", None) relations = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{RESULTS}/EC958/{a}/relations.tsv", sep="\t").assign(assembly=name) for a, name in ASSEMBLIES.items()], ignore_index=True) relations["reason"] = relations["reason"].fillna("–") pd.crosstab([relations["status"], relations["reason"]], relations["assembly"])[list(ASSEMBLIES.values())] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Wrong-IS cases A wrong-IS row only says the gene belongs to another IS's relation. `distance_error` helps judge each case: - **a few bp**: eris's IS sits where the truth IS is, so eris probably **misnamed** the IS (e.g. ISSen10 called IS629, IS26_2 called ISEc9); - **thousands of bp**: a **different IS further away** reports the same gene (e.g. ISEch14 at ~52 kb), which looks like a real neighbouring IS rather than a naming bug. ::: {#4ac68643 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} wrong_is = relations[relations["reason"] == "wrong_IS"] wrong_is[["assembly", "status", "side", "is_id", "locus_tag", "eris_target", "truth_distance", "eris_distance", "distance_error"]].sort_values(["assembly", "distance_error"]).reset_index(drop=True).fillna("") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: # Miss causes: not called vs not reported The old miss cause `gene` was a catch-all. It is now split, so every FN gets one of three miss causes, checked in this order ([eris-validation](https://github.com/Victoriasja18/eris-validation)): | Miss cause | Meaning | Where the bug is | |---|---|---| | `budget` | the `--hops 20` run finds it | eris stops walking too early | | `not_reported` | pyfgs **called** a gene that is the truth CDS (same strand, ≥ 50 % overlap), but eris never reports it as a flank of that IS on that side | eris's flank walk / reporting, or the IS (missed or misnamed) | | `not_called` | **no** gene pyfgs called is the truth CDS | gene calling (pyfgs), or a truth CDS that has no real ORF | How it works: eris's `_cds.fna` holds **every** gene pyfgs called on the assembly (6,291 on the real-reads GFA), not only the reported ones. All of them are placed on the reference with minimap2, the same way as the flank genes. If any of them matches the truth CDS, the gene was called, so the miss is `not_reported`; otherwise `not_called`. ::: {#0818b187 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} fn = relations[relations["status"] == "FN"] pd.crosstab([fn["miss_cause"]], fn["assembly"])[list(ASSEMBLIES.values())] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: What the split shows: - **Most GFA misses are `not_reported`** (26 of 37 simulated, 46 of 57 real-reads): pyfgs did call the gene, so the loss is in eris's flank walk and reporting (the collapsed repeat "roundabouts" below) or in the IS itself, not in gene calling. - **`not_called` stays about the same on every assembly** (15 complete, 9 simulated, 11 real-reads), so it is not caused by fragmentation. - **On the complete genome, 12 of the 15 `not_called` truth CDS are pseudogenes** (`pseudo = True`, mostly also partial), often genes broken by the IS itself. They have no intact ORF, so pyfgs cannot call them. The other 3 are tiny genes of 69–144 bp (ykiE, ykgR, a GNAT fragment). So most `not_called` misses come from the truth including pseudogenes, not from a pyfgs bug. ::: {#dc295c3a .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} complete = relations[(relations["assembly"] == ASSEMBLIES["complete"]) & (relations["miss_cause"] == "not_called")] span = complete["truth_location"].str.extract(r":(\d+)-(\d+)").astype(int) complete.assign(length_bp=span[1] - span[0])[["is_id", "side", "locus_tag", "gene", "product", "length_bp", "partial", "pseudo"]].reset_index(drop=True).fillna("") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

The truth and eris effects are still kept in `relations.tsv` (`truth_effect`, `eris_effect`) for reference. Side and distance scores did not change. # Why the GFA assemblies score worse | F1 (precision / recall), both sides | Complete | Simulated GFA | Real-reads GFA | |---|---|---|---| | Both sides | 0.65 (0.59 / 0.73) | 0.53 (0.47 / 0.61) | 0.50 (0.49 / 0.51) | | Distance band agreement | 0.71 | 0.63 | 0.62 | Why the GFA relations are missed (from extra analysis, not part of the workflow; the "not called" row now comes from the workflow's `not_called` miss cause, and matches): | Cause | Simulated (37 FN) | Real reads (57 FN) | |---|---|---| | Gene called by pyfgs, but no IS reports it as a flank, even at 20 hops | 17 | 38 | | Gene not called by pyfgs at all | 9 | 11 | | Gene reported next to a differently named IS | 7 | 7 | | IS not detected at all (ISSen10, ISSen1, IS5) | 6 | 4 | | Only found with 20 hops | 2 | 0 | | Wrong side | 2 | 1 | (The counts add to slightly more than the FN totals because a few misses fall into two categories.) - **Recall**: most lost genes sit on a contig **one link** away from the IS's contig. The IS involved are multi-copy (ISEc12, ISEc23, IS200C, IS1397, IS609); their contigs have 2–6× the normal depth (~33×), so one collapsed contig stands in for several copies (58 loci on the complete genome vs 35–36 on the GFAs). The single-copy contigs hanging off these "roundabouts" are often not reported as flanks. Since `--hops 20` does not recover them, this points to eris's flank walk / branch reporting in collapse mode, not to the hops budget. - **Precision**: about two thirds of the false nearest-flank calls are genes **shorter than 250 bp** (23 of 35 simulated, 22 of 34 real): small ORFs near contig ends that sit in front of the real gene. Another 4–7 are **unplaceable** fragments cut at contig ends.
